profile.address: Avenida de la Industria, 15, 28108 Alcobendas, Madrid, Spain
profile.reading:
DC03 is the third numbered building on DATA4's MAD01 campus in Alcobendas, on the northern edge of Madrid, Spain, at Avenida de la Industria 15. DATA4 is a French headquartered data center developer and operator, founded in 2006 and based in Paris, led by chief executive Olivier Micheli since November 2014. The company designs, builds, finances, and operates its own facilities rather than developing for third party landlords, and its Madrid MAD01 campus is positioned toward colocation customers, cloud providers, and carriers, distinct from the newer, more hyperscale oriented MAD02 campus the company is separately building at San Agustín del Guadalix north of the city.

A 2023 trade press account of DC03 breaking ground, sourced to the operator, put DC03 at 6.6 megawatts of IT capacity across 3,000 square meters of white space, describing the building as the third addition to a campus that already held DC01, at 14 megawatts of IT power across 6,500 square meters, and DC02, at 6.6 megawatts of IT capacity across another 3,000 square meters. That same account described the finished MAD01 campus, at full build out, as an eight hectare site hosting six buildings totaling 70 megawatts, with a pre-existing building on the DC03 site demolished within one month to clear the ground. DATA4's own current Madrid landing page, by contrast, describes MAD01 as a single 50 megawatt campus across 4 hectares, a smaller figure that likely reflects capacity commissioned to date rather than the six building design end state described in 2023. This registry records both figures with attribution rather than resolving the gap between them. No completion date or opening confirmation for DC03 itself was found this session, so its current operating status, more than three years after that groundbreaking, is not confirmed one way or the other.

DATA4's corporate ownership has changed twice since DC03 was announced. AXA Investment Managers Alternatives sold DATA4 to Brookfield Infrastructure in a deal worth 2.4 billion dollars, agreed in April 2023 and completed that August. Then, in August 2025, Brookfield brought in Arjun Infrastructure Partners and Interogo Holding as new shareholders in a stake sale covering DATA4's stabilised hyperscale portfolio in Paris, Milan, and Madrid, a combined 244 megawatts of contracted capacity that a Brookfield SEC filing valued at 3.6 billion dollars. Brookfield kept a stake alongside the new investors, and DATA4's own management team, still led by Micheli, continues to run the business day to day. Because the August 2025 release names Madrid generally rather than MAD01 specifically, it is not possible to say from that document alone whether DC03 sits inside the divested stabilised pool or remains a newer, still ramping asset outside it.

No tenant name for DC03 was found in any operator or trade source reviewed. No standby generator rating, utility interconnection figure, or onsite generation figure specific to this building was found either, only the campus level IT capacity figures already described above.

profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-05: prior version cited a banned aggregator site and a secondary magazine reprint, and carried an unsourced 15,000 sqm / three floor claim likely traced to that aggregator. Replaced with DCD English coverage of the DC03 groundbreaking (Apr 2023), which explicitly labels 6.6 MW as DC03 IT capacity across 3,000 sqm, and cross-checked against DATA4 own current Madrid page, which gives a smaller, campus-wide 50 MW / 4 ha figure. Corporate ownership history extended past the prior AXA-to-Brookfield-only account to include the August 2025 Arjun Infrastructure Partners / Interogo Holding stake sale into DATA4 stabilised Paris/Milan/Madrid portfolio (244 MW, $3.6bn per Brookfield SEC filing), sourced to DATA4 own press release and Interogo own release. No completion date for DC03 found. Sibling MAD01 rows (DC01 way/299384674, DC02 way/301156915, generic MAD1 way/1472194797) still carry the old aggregator-sourced text and AXA-only ownership framing as of this write and were not in this session scope for full rewrite.
profile.campus_power_note: The four power numbers for DATA4's MAD01 campus need to stay separate because two different totals are in circulation. DATA4's own current Madrid page states the MAD01 campus is 50 megawatts across 4 hectares. A 2023 trade press account of DC03's groundbreaking, sourced to the operator, instead describes an eight hectare site designed for six buildings totaling 70 megawatts once fully built, with DC01 at 14 MW IT capacity, DC02 at 6.6 MW IT capacity, and DC03 at 6.6 MW IT capacity confirmed individually. Both totals describe IT capacity, not utility interconnection ratings, standby generator ratings, or onsite generation figures, none of which were found published for this campus. This registry treats the 50 MW / 4 ha figure as the operator's current simplified marketing number and the 70 MW / six building / 8 ha figure as the more detailed design end state, and records both here rather than picking one.
